entities.name: PMID:25451608
observations: Randomized, blinded, saline-controlled crossover study in 25 healthy women (mean age 22.3 years).
Salmonella typhi vaccination induced low-grade inflammation, with leukocytosis increasing 100% and serum IL-6 increasing 670%.
Pain was assessed before and 6 hours after injection using pressure pain thresholds and thumbnail pain tolerance.
Baseline negative affectivity predicted reduced post-vaccination thumbnail pain tolerance (β = −0.57, p = .007), but not placebo-session tolerance (β = .25, p = .26).

entities.name: Negative affectivity-pain tolerance
observations: In healthy women exposed to Salmonella typhi vaccine, higher baseline negative affectivity predicted lower pain tolerance 6 hours later (β = −0.57, p = .007).
The association was not observed during saline placebo (β = .25, p = .26), supporting inflammation-specific prediction.
The evidence comes from one directly qualifying study; targeted searches found no additional study meeting all criteria.
